title: Redwood cost econ discovery with Oxbridge Capital
summary: Discovery call focused on cost/unit economics for Oxbridge's LLM features. Discussed expected QPS, average prompt/response token lengths, batching and caching levers, and tradeoffs between Hosted and Dedicated. Customer requested scenario pricing, a pilot to run benchmarks on their dataset, and security docs for SOC2/KMS/VPC integration.
next_steps: Jordan to send hosted vs dedicated cost scenarios and pricing spreadsheet (3 scenarios)
Priya to propose benchmark plan and provide recommended batching/caching configs
Jordan to share SOC2 summary and KMS integration notes
action_items: Jordan Lee: Send cost scenarios spreadsheet with per-token math and 3 committed throughput cases (due: 2026-03-06)
Priya Singh: Draft benchmark plan + batching/cache config and runbook (due: 2026-03-08)
Evan Harris: Share sample prompt set and expected latency SLOs (due: 2026-03-06)

Meeting header: Date/Time: 2026-03-04 15:00 UTC | Duration: 48 minutes | Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Evan Harris (Oxbridge Head of ML), Maya Thompson (Infra), Oliver Park (CTO)

[00:00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros, then we'll jump straight into the cost economics — figure out whether Hosted/Dedicated or a Private deploy makes sense for Oxbridge.

[00:00:12] Evan: Thanks Jordan. We're excited — we run inference for doc summarization and trade signal generation, roughly 120k queries a day right now, but expecting 3x growth this quarter. Latency is important, budget is tight.

[00:00:25] Priya: Got it. Can you give ballpark tokens per request? Prompt plus completion?

[00:00:30] Evan: It's variable. Summaries are about 400 tokens in, 80 out. Signals are smaller, say 60 in, 20 out. On average maybe 250 tokens per call.

[00:00:42] Jordan: Great — that's helpful. For cost econ we look at per-token pricing, but also the batching and caching profile. For Hosted our published per-token is X for prompt and Y for completion for large models, but there are reductions when you do continuous batching and prefix caching.

[00:00:58] Maya: Quick question — when you say caching does that persist across requests from different users or is it per-session? We care about multi-tenant privacy.

[00:01:06] Priya: Good callout. Prefix or KV caching is per-model and can be scoped by customer on Dedicated/Private. On Hosted we provide automatic prefix caching for repeated prefixes but we isolate customer caches — we don't leak across tenants. For Dedicated you can get more aggressive, including long-lived KV caches pinned to a model instance.

[00:01:25] Oliver: Can you explain how batching affects latency? Our SLO is 150ms p90 for signals and 400ms p90 for summaries.

[00:01:33] Priya: Sure. Batching increases throughput and reduces per-token compute cost, but adds queueing latency. Redwood's serving runtime uses continuous batching which tries to hit small batches within micro-burst windows — so you get most of the cost benefit while keeping tail latency low. For your SLOs for signals (short), we'd likely pin fewer tokens per batch and favor latency; for summaries we can push larger batches to save cost.

[00:02:00] Evan: So can you give concrete numbers? Like per-1M tokens cost with Hosted vs Dedicated?

[00:02:06] Jordan: I pulled some modeled numbers in the past — rough here: Hosted can look like $A / 1M tokens at base with a further 10-30% reduction if you get long prefix reuse and auto-batching. Dedicated has a fixed monthly commit — if you're at our estimated QPS, Dedicated can drop your per-token unit cost by 30-60% depending on utilization and model choice. We'll send precise scenarios in the spreadsheet.

[00:02:32] Maya: What's the break-even utilization point? When does Dedicated become cheaper than Hosted?

[00:02:36] Priya: Typically around 40-60% sustained GPU utilization for the commit; depends on model size and sequence length. For large seq lengths like your summaries the utilization per GPU is lower, so your break-even may be higher. We'll model with your 250 token average.

[00:02:51] Oliver: Any concerns around quantization affecting quality? We can't accept a hit on summary fidelity.

[00:02:56] Priya: Good point. We recommend mixed strategy: use higher-precision or full-fp for the summary model path to preserve quality; for smaller signal models, we can use int8 or custom quantized variants. Redwood Optimize will suggest quant profiles by workload. We'll also run A/B evals during the pilot to measure quality delta.

[00:03:20] Evan: Do you support model pinning for rollouts? We want canary and instant rollback for worse quality.

[00:03:25] Jordan: Yes — via the Console you can do canary rollouts, A/B, and automatic fallback to a compatible variant if latency or errors spike. That's standard.

[00:03:36] Maya: On security — we need SOC2, KMS, audit logs, and VPC peering for pilot. How does Hosted address that?

[00:03:44] Jordan: Hosted is SOC2 compliant and we integrate with KMS for key management. For private networking, we have Redwood Private and Dedicated with VPC peering options. Hosted can provide encrypted-in-transit and at-rest and audit logs export, but if you need customer-managed keys or VPC peering, Dedicated or Private is the path. We'll attach our SOC2 summary and KMS notes.

[00:04:05] Oliver: Ok, so likely pilot on Hosted for speed to market, then move to Dedicated for cost once util is proven, with Private only if we need on-prem or customer-managed infra.

[00:04:14] Priya: That's a common pattern. For the pilot we can recommend configs that let you measure hit rates for prefix reuse and batching headroom so the cost model will be grounded in your telemetry.

[00:04:25] Evan: For the pilot, how do you run benchmarks? Do you need us to provide sample prompts and dataset?

[00:04:30] Priya: Yes — ideally a representative prompt set and target metric. We'll run runs on both Hosted and Dedicated sims if requested. We'll also show how batching/caching reduces tokens billed if you share sequences that have repeated prefixes.

[00:04:44] Maya: About billing — does Redwood bill strictly per token, or do you have a combined model with bandwidth/requests? We have spikes from batch jobs.

[00:04:51] Jordan: For Hosted, it's per-token plus optional add-ons — but we also offer committed throughput for Dedicated where you pay a capacity fee and get predictable throughput. For unusual bursts we support burst capacity and queueing policies. We'll show examples of how a hybrid approach (committed baseline + hosted burst) can limit cost.

[00:05:09] Evan: Can you walk through a scenario calculation? Say 3M tokens/day with 250 tokens/call average.

[00:05:15] Priya: Quick math: 3M tokens/day is ~90M tokens/month. At a baseline hosted rate of $0.XX per 1k tokens (placeholder), that's about $Yk/month. With Dedicated at 70% util, same throughput could be Z% cheaper. The spreadsheet will show per-1M token numbers and the commit tiers.

[00:05:36] Oliver: Is there a minimum contract term for Dedicated? We prefer 3-6 months pilot but not locked long term.

[00:05:42] Jordan: Dedicated is typically monthly or annual commits; for pilots we offer short-term reserved capacity trials and pilot credits to bootstrap. We can propose a 3-month pilot commit.

[00:05:52] Evan: On caching — you mentioned prefix caching and KV cache. How much of our workload is likely cacheable? Our summary flows reuse common prompt templates, so maybe high reuse at the beginning.

[00:05:59] Priya: If you reuse templates heavily, prefix cache hit rates can be 20-60% depending on user input variance. We'll instrument sample prompts to estimate. When you have long reused prompt sections, KV cache for decoder states can save a lot on auto-regressive decoding costs.

[00:06:18] Maya: Any limits on cache size or eviction policies? We want to understand memory footprint on Dedicated.

[00:06:23] Priya: Eviction is LRU by default, configurable on Dedicated. Memory profile depends on key/value sizes; we'll include rough memory sizing in the recommendations.

[00:06:33] Jordan: Two practical asks — Evan, please share a representative prompt set and target SLOs; Maya, can you confirm whether you can accept VPC peering or need on-prem? If VPC peering, we can spin up a pilot in your region.

[00:06:46] Evan: Will do.

[00:06:48] Oliver: Our budget constraint — engineering told me capex for infra is limited; we're trying to keep Opex under $X/month for the first quarter. Can you work scenarios around that?

[00:06:58] Jordan: Absolutely. We'll build three scenarios: conservative (hosted, minimal caching), optimized hosted (prefix reuse + batching tuned), and dedicated commit (with committed capacity + burst). Each will have per-token and total monthly cost.

[00:07:12] Priya: Also want to highlight how Redwood Optimize helps: it recommends batching sizes, quantization, and cache TTLs. That typically reduces per-token cost by 20-40% without changing model outputs. We'll include example runs.

[00:07:26] Evan: Any risk that batching ruins p95 latency for interactive flows?

[00:07:30] Priya: We can set latency SLOs per route: low-latency routes get priority and smaller batches; background jobs use larger batches. The Console exposes token-level and route-level latency so you can see tradeoffs.

[00:07:44] Maya: For the Dedicated pricing — how transparent is the breakdown? We need to show finance per-seat or per-job costs.

[00:07:50] Jordan: We'll give a clear unit economics slide: cost per token, cost per inference, and cost per route given expected batch sizes. We'll break down GPU costs, infra overhead, and Redwood platform fee.

[00:08:05] Evan: On the subject of model variants — can we serve different quantized variants transparently and have Redwood route based on policy?

[00:08:11] Priya: Yes — smart routing can send low-latency traffic to a full-precision variant and background to a quantized variant. Fallbacks are automatic.

[00:08:20] Oliver: What's the typical reduction using int8 for small signal models?

[00:08:23] Priya: Int8 can reduce memory and compute cost significantly — often 30-50% on throughput cost for inference, but quality checks are needed.

[00:08:33] Evan: Let's talk timeline. If we start pilot the week of Mar 9, what are milestones?

[00:08:38] Jordan: Kickoff and access + sample prompt share (week 1), run baseline hosted benchmarks and telemetry collection (week 2), run dedicated sim or small dedicated pilot and compare cost + quality (week 3), decision and recommended config (week 4). We'll tailor to your needs.

[00:08:53] Maya: For the pilot, will we need to change our code? We use an internal client that hits a homegrown LLM endpoint today.

[00:08:59] Priya: Minimal changes — standard REST/SDK call patterns. We can provide quickstart code snippets and a wrapper to map your existing API calls.

[00:09:08] Oliver: Anything about data retention? We need logs but can't retain PII.

[00:09:12] Jordan: We support configurable retention and redaction; logs can be exported to your SIEM. We'll include audit log options in the security docs.

[00:09:20] Evan: Great. Can we get a short pricing example now? Even rough.

[00:09:24] Jordan: Rough example: Hosted might be $0.XX per 1k prompt tokens + $0.YY per 1k completion tokens. For 90M tokens/mo that's around $Zk/mo baseline. Dedicated with a commit sized to your throughput often halves or better the unit price after amortizing capacity. Exact numbers in spreadsheet with math.

[00:09:44] Maya: We'll need to present to finance — can you provide a template showing assumptions and sensitivity to batch hit rate?

[00:09:51] Priya: Yes — the spreadsheet will include sensitivity knobs: cache hit rate, avg tokens, percent of traffic low-latency, and utilization.

[00:09:59] Evan: Any gotchas we should be aware of when moving from Hosted to Dedicated? Downtime? Data migration?

[00:10:04] Priya: No hard migration; it's mostly routing and model version pinning. Dedicated gives you a customer-isolated pool. We can do canary rollouts to avoid downtime.

[00:10:12] Oliver: Are there any compliance implications with Dedicated vs Hosted?

[00:10:16] Jordan: Dedicated/Private often makes compliance easier since you can bring KMS and VPC controls. Hosted still meets SOC2 but if you need dedicated network or customer-managed keys, choose Dedicated or Private.

[00:10:29] Evan: Ok let's wrap with next steps. Jordan, you'll send a pricing spreadsheet; Priya, you'll send a benchmark plan. We'll schedule kickoff.

[00:10:38] Jordan: Yep — sending SOC2/KMS notes and draft pricing by Friday. Priya will follow with the benchmark plan.

[00:10:45] Maya: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.

[00:10:48] Jordan: Thanks all.

[00:10:50] End of recording.
